newsitem.title: UK: UK's European Aviation looks to hushkit BAC 1-11s.
newsitem.headline: UK's European Aviation looks to hushkit BAC 1-11s.

text.p: British airline European Aviation Air Charter said it has signed a contract with U.S. company Quiet Nacelle Corporation aimed at developing "Stage 3" hushkits for its fleet of BAC 1-11 aircraft.
But the Bournemouth International airport-based carrier would give no financial details.
European currently operates 15 1-11s under its UK aircraft operating certificate (AOC), all powered by "Stage 2" Rolls-Royce Spey engines, which are noisier than the "Stage 3" versions.
The carrier said it also owns 12 more 1-11s in differing conditions that do not meet current noise regulations.

"Engine components have been shipped to (Miami, Florida-based) Quiet Nacelle in order for them to assemble a prototype proof-of-concept hushkit," said European Aviation managing director Trevor Whetter.
He added that after initial tests, the new module would be fitted to an EAAC 1-11 at Bournemouth, probably in September, and then test flown for 40 hours.
No timescale for application of the hushkits to European's aircraft was given.

Whetter said that European Aviation was also currently talking with a number of UK design companies regarding the appointment of an approved UK project authority which would hold the hushkit's supplemental type certificate.

Additionally, he said that under the deal with Quiet Nacelle, EAAC subsidiary European Aviation Maintenance would undertake installation of huskits for 1-11 500 series and possibly earlier series of the aircraft worldwide. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
